quote.text: Men, it has been well said, think in herds; it will be seen that they go mad in herds, while they only recover their senses slowly, and one by one.
quote.author: Charles Mackay, Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds (preface, 1852 ed.)

macro.title: What It Means — VWRA, Bonds, Gold & BTC

reads.label: VWRA (held)
reads.text: near its record; a softer barrel and a softer dollar are a relief, but Wednesday's Warsh statement is the swing, and this week's mega-cap earnings move it more than the Fed.

reads.label: Global bonds (held)
reads.text: the −4bp in the 10-year and an easier dollar both help; the enemy remains a hawkish surprise or an oil re-spike.

reads.label: Gold (read only)
reads.text: near a record and decoupling higher on the softer dollar even as oil fell — the cleanest hedge on the board.

reads.label: Bitcoin (read only)
reads.text: range-bound near $65k, trading as high-beta risk, not gold's twin. The two he holds stay VWRA and global bonds; the two he only reads stay gold and BTC.

stories.headline: The Guns Stay Quiet, and the Barrel Loses Its Nerve
stories.dek: A fourth day without a strike, an Omani draft that still needs a signature, and a market that decided not to wait for one. Brent fell 8.7 per cent on Monday — the sharpest drop since the war began — as traders sold the fear faster than the diplomats could earn it.

stories.headline: The Biggest Open Model Ever, and Almost No One Can Run It
stories.dek: Moonshot shipped Kimi K3 on schedule, and the independent scores are in: an intelligence index around 57, top-three or -four in the world, Opus-4.8-class at a fraction of the price. It is also 2.8 trillion parameters, hallucinates more than its predecessor, and is unloadable by design. A flag planted, not a tool delivered.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Portfolio Lens
stories.headline: The Barrel Falls, and the Hike Tail Thins
stories.dek: One number drove the whole board this week: Brent down 8.7 per cent. That single slide loosened the dollar, cooled the priced odds of a Fed hike, and let gold decouple higher on the softer greenback — even as Singapore's own bank leaned the other way and tightened. Market explanation, not investment advice.

stories.headline: The Bank Was Meant to Hold. It Tightened.
stories.dek: Almost every desk on the Street had pencilled in a hold for Monday's statement. Instead the Monetary Authority of Singapore steepened the slope of its currency band a second straight time — a small move, but a hawkish surprise, and a bet that the inflation still in the pipe outweighs the oil shock already fading.

stories.headline: Nine Thousand Plots Hit the Launch Pad
stories.dek: The story on the ground is no longer the price of money — it's the volume of land. The government's confirmed release for 2026 now runs to 9,320 units, more than half again the ten-year average, and the newest launch cleared just 54 per cent on its opening day. The pipeline, not demand, is setting the pace.

stories.headline: Sony Puts a Price on Internal RAW
stories.dek: The FX5 we flagged at announcement now has a number and a ship date: US$4,899 for the body, mid-August, with 5K Open Gate and 16-bit internal RAW — a first for the FX line. Below it, a screenless recovery band goes at Whoop for two hundred dollars and no subscription, and Samsung names its glasses without daring to price them.

stories.headline: The Assistant That Lives in Your House Grows Up
stories.dek: With Home Assistant 2026.8 now in beta and due the first Wednesday of August, the interesting change isn't a headline feature — it's the quiet maturing of the fully-local voice stack. Ollama sub-entries, a Whisper-and-Piper pipeline, and a Lutron integration that talks to the hardware without the cloud: the migrator's payoff, arriving in pieces.

stories.headline: A Turntable Dressed as a Beatles Sleeve
stories.dek: Clearaudio has built a deck to mark the 60th anniversary of Revolver — monochrome, like the record's cover, and bundled with a fresh pressing of the album itself. At US$17,900 it is a beautiful object and an honest question: how much of the price is engineering, and how much is the sleeve?

stories.headline: The Verdict Is Written, and Sealed Until Tonight
stories.dek: Reviews of Spider-Man: Brand New Day are embargoed until nine o'clock tonight, Singapore time — so as this issue goes out, the critic score does not yet exist. The social first-reactions are ecstatic; the prediction markets are pricing a low-nineties. Both are guesses, and the film opens here Wednesday. Meanwhile, Nolan quietly owns the big screens.

stories.headline: Your Child Sleeps an Hour Less Than You Think
stories.dek: Ask a parent whether their primary-schooler gets enough sleep and most say yes. Strap a movement sensor to the same child's wrist and the yes collapses. In one study, 83 per cent of children "met" the sleep guideline by parental estimate — and under 15 per cent actually did. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: A Planet Found by Tasting Its Air
stories.dek: Some worlds are too faint to photograph. Astronomers found a new one anyway — a gas giant orbiting Beta Pictoris, 100 times dimmer than its known sibling — not by seeing it, but by reading the carbon monoxide, water and methane in its atmosphere. Two teams caught the same ghost, independently.

stories.headline: Opposites Don't Attract. Idealising Does.
stories.dek: A study across 74 countries and 41,606 people tested the old questions — do we want a partner like us, or better than us? The answer splits by trait. For kindness and looks, happiness peaks when you rate your partner above yourself. For politics and religion, only actual similarity will do.

stories.headline: Ninety Minutes of Lifting. No Bonus for More.
stories.dek: A pooled analysis of 147,374 adults, tracked up to thirty years, found the longevity return on strength training concentrated in a narrow band: 90 to 119 minutes a week bought most of the benefit, and past about two hours there was none. For a mid-40s reader, that is permission, not pressure. Not medical advice.

stories.headline: A Sprint Comes to Marina Bay
stories.dek: The Grand Prix year just got a full Saturday race and a bigger bill — and around it, the autumn concert calendar hardens into a set of real decisions about which nights to hold.

stories.headline: Mechanical Healing
stories.dek: In eighteen months, a craft of ironing plastic beads into pixel-art went from a niche hobby to a national craze in China to a price war that is shuttering shops this month. The West has not written it up yet. By the time it does, the boom will be a bust — and that speed is the actual story.
